origin:
Cadillac Racing's amateur origins are deeply intertwined with the passion of a group of engineers at General Motors' Detroit headquarters in the early 2000s. Dissatisfied with simply designing road cars, they sought to prove the performance capabilities of Cadillac beyond the showroom floor. They started small, initially entering local autocross events and track days with heavily modified CTS sedans, funded largely out of their own pockets and with the blessing of sympathetic managers who saw the potential marketing value. Their early efforts, while not always successful, attracted attention and a small but enthusiastic following within GM.

The team's breakthrough moment came at the 2005 SCCA National Championship Runoffs at Mid-Ohio. Against seasoned privateer teams with far more resources, the Cadillac Racing entry, still largely assembled in a corner of a GM engineering workshop, managed a podium finish. This unexpected result caught the eye of upper management, leading to a modest but crucial increase in factory support, allowing them to upgrade their equipment and compete in select professional events. While a full-fledged factory program remained a distant dream, Cadillac Racing had proven its potential and cemented its place as a plucky underdog with serious potential.
philosophy: Cadillac Racing operates on the principle of leveraging factory engineering expertise to overcome resource limitations. Their approach to car development emphasizes reliability and incremental improvements, focusing on maximizing the potential of existing components rather than pursuing radical innovation. The team culture is one of camaraderie and dedication, fostered by a shared love of motorsport and a determination to prove that passion and ingenuity can triumph over pure financial might.
achievements: Podium finish at the 2005 SCCA National Championship Runoffs (Touring 1)
Multiple class wins in regional SCCA events
Consistent top-10 finishes in select professional GT races
Development of several performance-enhancing technologies that were later integrated into Cadillac production models

teamPrincipal.name: Michael Davies
teamPrincipal.background: Davies, a former GM engineer who was instrumental in the team's initial formation, is known for his calm demeanor and ability to inspire his team. He balances technical expertise with strong leadership, fostering a collaborative environment where every member feels valued.

keyFigures.name: Sarah Jenkins
keyFigures.description: Jenkins, a rising star in automotive engineering, oversees the team's technical strategy and car development. Her innovative solutions and meticulous attention to detail have been crucial to the team's success.

headquarters: Cadillac Racing is based out of a modest workshop located within the General Motors Technical Center in Warren, Michigan. Their facilities are basic but functional, providing the team with access to GM's extensive engineering resources.
fanBase: Cadillac Racing's fanbase consists primarily of GM employees, local racing enthusiasts, and loyal Cadillac owners who appreciate the team's dedication to showcasing the brand's performance capabilities. They are known for their enthusiastic support and unwavering belief in the team's potential.
